```{r, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning=FALSE)
# plotly.js from the CDN, so the site's pages don't each copy it

```
### Basic Filled Area Plot

To make an area plot with interior filling set `fill` to `"tozeroy"` in the call for the second trace.
For more informations and options about the `fill` option checkout `go_scatter()`

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

density <- density(ggplot2::diamonds$carat)

go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(x = density$x, y = density$y, mode = "lines", fill = "tozeroy") |>
  update_layout(
    xaxis = go_xaxis(title = "Carat"),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "Density")
  )
```

### Filled Area Plot with Multiple Traces

To make a filled area plot set `fill` to `"tozeroy"`.

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

diamonds <- ggplot2::diamonds
diamonds1 <- diamonds[which(diamonds$cut == "Fair"), ]
density1 <- density(diamonds1$carat)

diamonds2 <- diamonds[which(diamonds$cut == "Ideal"), ]
density2 <- density(diamonds2$carat)

go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = density1$x,
    y = density1$y,
    mode = "lines",
    name = "Fair cut",
    fill = "tozeroy"
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = density2$x,
    y = density2$y,
    mode = "lines",
    name = "Ideal cut",
    fill = "tozeroy"
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    xaxis = go_xaxis(title = "Carat"),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "Density")
  )
```

### Selecting Hover Points 

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2),
    y = c(0, 1, 2, 1, 0),
    fill = "toself",
    fillcolor = "#ab63fa",
    hoveron = "points+fills",
    marker = go_scatter_marker(color = "#ab63fa"),
    line = go_scatter_line(color = "#ab63fa"),
    text = "Points + Fills",
    hoverinfo = "text"
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = c(3, 3.5, 4, 4.5, 5),
    y = c(0, 1, 2, 1, 0),
    fill = "toself",
    fillcolor = "#e763fa",
    hoveron = "points",
    marker = go_scatter_marker(color = "#e763fa"),
    line = go_scatter_line(color = "#e763fa"),
    text = "Points only",
    hoverinfo = "text"
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "hover on <i>points</i> or <i>fill</i>",
    xaxis = go_xaxis(range = c(0, 5.2)),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(range = c(0, 3))
  )
```

### Custom Colors

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

diamonds <- ggplot2::diamonds
diamonds1 <- diamonds[which(diamonds$cut == "Fair"), ]
density1 <- density(diamonds1$carat)

diamonds2 <- diamonds[which(diamonds$cut == "Ideal"), ]
density2 <- density(diamonds2$carat)

go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = density1$x,
    y = density1$y,
    mode = "lines",
    name = "Fair cut",
    fill = "tozeroy",
    fillcolor = "rgba(168, 216, 234, 0.5)",
    line = go_scatter_line(width = 0.5)
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = density2$x,
    y = density2$y,
    mode = "lines",
    name = "Ideal cut",
    fill = "tozeroy",
    fillcolor = "rgba(255, 212, 96, 0.5)"
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    xaxis = go_xaxis(title = "Carat"),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "Density")
  )
```

### Area Plot without Lines

To make an area plot without lines set `mode` to `"none"`.

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

diamonds <- ggplot2::diamonds
diamonds1 <- diamonds[which(diamonds$cut == "Fair"), ]
density1 <- density(diamonds1$carat)

diamonds2 <- diamonds[which(diamonds$cut == "Ideal"), ]
density2 <- density(diamonds2$carat)

go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = density1$x,
    y = density1$y,
    mode = "none",
    name = "Fair cut",
    fill = "tozeroy",
    fillcolor = "rgba(168, 216, 234, 0.5)"
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = density2$x,
    y = density2$y,
    mode = "none",
    name = "Ideal cut",
    fill = "tozeroy",
    fillcolor = "rgba(255, 212, 96, 0.5)"
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    xaxis = go_xaxis(title = "Carat"),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "Density")
  )
```

### Interior Filling for Area Chart

To make an area plot with interior filling set `fill` to `"tonexty"` in the call for the second trace.
For more informations and options about the `fill` option checkout `go_scatter()`

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

month <- c("January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July",
           "August", "September", "October", "November", "December")
high_2014 <- c(28.8, 28.5, 37.0, 56.8, 69.7, 79.7, 78.5, 77.8, 74.1, 62.6, 45.3, 39.9)
low_2014 <- c(12.7, 14.3, 18.6, 35.5, 49.9, 58.0, 60.0, 58.6, 51.7, 45.2, 32.2, 29.1)
data <- data.frame(month, high_2014, low_2014)
data$average_2014 <- rowMeans(data[, c("high_2014", "low_2014")])

#The default order will be alphabetized unless specified as below:
data$month <- factor(data$month, levels = data[["month"]])

data |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~month,
    y = ~high_2014,
    mode = "lines",
    line = go_scatter_line(color = "rgba(0,100,80,1)"),
    showlegend = FALSE,
    name = "High 2014"
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~month,
    y = ~low_2014,
    mode = "lines",
    fill = "tonexty",
    fillcolor = "rgba(0,100,80,0.2)",
    line = go_scatter_line(color = "rgba(0,100,80,1)"),
    showlegend = FALSE,
    name = "Low 2014"
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "High and Low Temperatures in New York",
    paper_bgcolor = "rgb(255,255,255)",
    plot_bgcolor = "rgb(229,229,229)",
    xaxis = go_xaxis(
      title = "Months",
      gridcolor = "rgb(255,255,255)",
      showgrid = TRUE,
      showline = FALSE,
      showticklabels = TRUE,
      tickcolor = "rgb(127,127,127)",
      ticks = "outside",
      zeroline = FALSE
    ),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(
      title = "Temperature (degrees F)",
      gridcolor = "rgb(255,255,255)",
      showgrid = TRUE,
      showline = FALSE,
      showticklabels = TRUE,
      tickcolor = "rgb(127,127,127)",
      ticks = "outside",
      zeroline = FALSE
    )
  )
```

### Stacked Area Chart with Original Values

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

data <- t(USPersonalExpenditure)
data <- data.frame("year" = rownames(data), data)

data |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~year,
    y = ~Food.and.Tobacco,
    name = "Food and Tobacco",
    mode = "none",
    stackgroup = "one",
    fillcolor = "#F5FF8D"
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~year,
    y = ~Household.Operation,
    name = "Household Operation",
    mode = "none",
    stackgroup = "one",
    fillcolor = "#50CB86"
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~year,
    y = ~Medical.and.Health,
    name = "Medical and Health",
    mode = "none",
    stackgroup = "one",
    fillcolor = "#4C74C9"
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~year,
    y = ~Personal.Care,
    name = "Personal Care",
    mode = "none",
    stackgroup = "one",
    fillcolor = "#700961"
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~year,
    y = ~Private.Education,
    name = "Private Education",
    mode = "none",
    stackgroup = "one",
    fillcolor = "#312F44"
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "United States Personal Expenditures by Categories",
    xaxis = go_xaxis(title = "", showgrid = FALSE),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(
      title = "Expenditures (in billions of dollars)",
      showgrid = FALSE
    )
  )
```

### Stacked Area Chart with Cumulative Values

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

data <- t(USPersonalExpenditure)
data <- data.frame("year" = rownames(data), data)

data |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~year,
    y = ~Food.and.Tobacco,
    name = "Food and Tobacco",
    mode = "none",
    stackgroup = "one",
    groupnorm = "percent",
    fillcolor = "#F5FF8D"
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~year,
    y = ~Household.Operation,
    name = "Household Operation",
    mode = "none",
    stackgroup = "one",
    fillcolor = "#50CB86"
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~year,
    y = ~Medical.and.Health,
    name = "Medical and Health",
    mode = "none",
    stackgroup = "one",
    fillcolor = "#4C74C9"
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~year,
    y = ~Personal.Care,
    name = "Personal Care",
    mode = "none",
    stackgroup = "one",
    fillcolor = "#700961"
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~year,
    y = ~Private.Education,
    name = "Private Education",
    mode = "none",
    stackgroup = "one",
    fillcolor = "#312F44"
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "United States Personal Expenditures by Categories",
    xaxis = go_xaxis(title = "", showgrid = FALSE),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(
      title = "Proportion from the Total Expenditures",
      showgrid = FALSE,
      ticksuffix = "%"
    )
  )
```

#Reference

See `go_scatter()` (`fill` and `stackgroup`) for more information and chart attribute options!
